title: Rudolf Blaschka 1892 — Tempe field selection, preservation choice and media assignment
purpose: Extend pass19-20 by asking whether selective conversion began only later in Hosterwitz or was already built into fieldwork at Tempe. The Tempe letters show an earlier filtering stage: abundant vegetation was reduced to a subset judged useful, showy, characteristic and practically handleable, and different references were assigned different preservation/media routes.

primary_sources.direct_finding: Rudolf describes Tempe as the first western destination and says he and Ganong expect to remain a few days because the vegetation provides abundant good study material.
primary_sources.mechanism: site duration responds to reference yield

primary_sources.direct_finding: Rudolf says that after much drawing on the previous day he now has ten interesting species. He describes a carriage excursion into the desert with Ganong, notes abundant unfamiliar vegetation, and says he has already drawn two additional smaller cactus species that day.
primary_sources.mechanism: drawing converts field abundance into a counted working set
primary_sources.guard: Do not equate the ten 'interesting species' automatically with the later count of twenty-five 'useful' species; the categories and time windows differ.

direct_findings: A group excursion went by rented wagon to mountains/desert a few miles outside Tempe.
The party carried holders to keep plants fresh.
Rudolf drew flowers of about four cactus species and dug up young examples of those species to take with him.
He explicitly says these cacti did not need to be preserved in alcohol; he intended instead to send them from California to Hosterwitz.
He deliberately did not collect the dangerous 'Jumping Cactus' because of its hooked spines.
He found a striking Delphinium in a small desert patch and drew it immediately after returning in the afternoon.
He says a large proportion of desert plants were very small, so most were ignored; the party selected the most showy and most characteristic plants, giving twenty-five species useful to them.
He expected to finish all his Tempe sketches before leaving for Maricopa and California.
primary_sources.mechanism: explicit field filtering plus medium-specific preservation/transport choice

sequence: evaluate usefulness / showiness / characteristic form / handling feasibility
assign a reference medium or preservation route

media_and_handling_routes_visible.evidence: ten interesting species from recent drawing by 20 April; cactus flowers and Delphinium drawn by 22 April
media_and_handling_routes_visible.function: retains visible/formal information without requiring continuous carriage of the whole plant

media_and_handling_routes_visible.evidence: 22 April excursion equipped with holders to keep plants fresh
media_and_handling_routes_visible.function: keeps plant material usable between field encounter and near-term study/drawing

media_and_handling_routes_visible.route: live uprooted specimen + planned postal/freight dispatch
media_and_handling_routes_visible.evidence: young cactus examples dug up and intended for shipment from California to Hosterwitz
media_and_handling_routes_visible.function: moves living reference material across the split workshop

media_and_handling_routes_visible.route: alcohol preservation considered but rejected for selected cacti
media_and_handling_routes_visible.evidence: Rudolf explicitly contrasts live shipment with preserving those cacti in alcohol
media_and_handling_routes_visible.function: reveals a preservation menu rather than one default transport form

media_and_handling_routes_visible.evidence: independent Harvard University Herbaria records preserve multiple Ganong-Blaschka Tempe specimens dated 18-22 April 1892
media_and_handling_routes_visible.function: creates a durable institutional reference lineage distinct from drawings and living dispatches
media_and_handling_routes_visible.guard: The Tempe letters cited here do not individually identify each surviving HUH sheet; this route is established by joining the correspondence to the independent herbarium records.

media_and_handling_routes_visible.evidence: most tiny desert plants were ignored; Jumping Cactus was deliberately not collected
media_and_handling_routes_visible.function: absence from the transported packet can be actively produced in the field

two_stage_selective_conversion.stage_1_field: Field selection and media assignment: abundant vegetation is reduced to a practically and representationally useful packet.
two_stage_selective_conversion.stage_2_workshop: Workshop reactivation: only some returned references later become drawings, analytical studies or glass models.
two_stage_selective_conversion.claim: Selective conversion therefore begins before transport from Arizona. Transportable reference forms are produced through field choices about what is worth retaining and how it can survive or remain usable.

temporal_source_criticality.letter_evidence: On 22 April Rudolf refers to excursions 'today and Tuesday', indicating at least two named group excursions on 22 and 19 April.
temporal_source_criticality.result: Herbarium specimen dates should not be mapped one-to-one onto the two named group-excursion dates. They may register collecting outside group excursions, Ganong's collecting, preparation/label dates, or other field episodes.
temporal_source_criticality.guard: Keep mobility clock, drawing/work clock, specimen-label clock and dispatch clock distinct until sheet images and complete itinerary evidence are joined.

research_claims: The field did not output an undifferentiated mass of plants; it output selected references in different material/media states.
Usefulness was an explicit historical category in Rudolf's own account: many plants were ignored, while showy and characteristic forms were selected.
Material properties affected medium choice: cactus survival made live shipment possible, dangerous spines could prevent collection, and temporary holders kept other material fresh.
Portability was produced through selection and representation before later packing and freight operations.
The split workshop was coupled by heterogeneous reference forms, not by a single specimen channel.
article_consequence: Pass19-20 showed selective workshop reactivation and the need to separate reference continuity from name continuity. Pass21 moves the selection mechanism upstream: the reference corpus itself was already filtered and materially differentiated in the field. A stronger article architecture can therefore follow two gates: field selection/media assignment, then workshop reactivation/model production.
map_decision: No new public geographic lines. Tempe should eventually support a detail-layer media-switch diagram showing encounter -> select/reject -> draw/fresh/live/pressed -> dispatch/retain, rather than additional route geometry.
next_steps: Retrieve the complete Ganong-Blaschka 1892 HUH collector-level result set and inspect original sheet-label dates/names.
Search the Tempe and immediate California letters for the actual dispatch of the live cactus packet and whether Hosterwitz confirms receipt/growth.
Crosswalk the twenty-five useful Tempe species, where identifiable, against Corning preparatory drawings, HUH sheets and later model numbers.
Keep the ten-species and twenty-five-species counts separate unless an intermediate letter establishes cumulative identity.
Test whether comparable explicit selection language appears in Jamaica and San Diego, which would show whether the Tempe mechanism was local or a recurrent field method.
